[Canada's waterways](/wiki/List_of_longest_rivers_of_Canada "List of longest rivers of Canada") host forty-seven rivers of at least 600 kilometres (370 mi) in length, with the two longest being the [Mackenzie River](/wiki/Mackenzie_River "Mackenzie River"), that begins at [Great Slave Lake](/wiki/Great_Slave_Lake "Great Slave Lake") and ends in the [Arctic Ocean](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean"), with its drainage basin covering a large part of northwestern Canada, and the [Saint Lawrence River](/wiki/Saint_Lawrence_River "Saint Lawrence River"), which drains the [Great Lakes](/wiki/Great_Lakes "Great Lakes") into the [Gulf of St. Lawrence](/wiki/Gulf_of_St._Lawrence "Gulf of St. Lawrence") ending in the [Atlantic Ocean](/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean"). The [31 colleges](/wiki/Colleges_of_the_University_of_Cambridge "Colleges of the University of Cambridge") of the present-day University of Cambridge were originally an incidental feature of the university; no college within the University of Cambridge is as old as the university itself. The colleges within the university were initially endowed fellowships of scholars. There were also institutions without endowments, called hostels, which were gradually absorbed by the colleges over the centuries, and they have left some traces, including the naming of Garret Hostel Lane and [Garret Hostel Bridge](/wiki/Garret_Hostel_Bridge "Garret Hostel Bridge"), a street and bridge in Cambridge.[[24]](#cite_note-25)

The award was presented for the first time on February 5, 2023, at the [65th Annual Grammy Awards](/wiki/65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards"). Zeilinger is also interested to extend quantum mechanics into the macroscopic domain. In the early 1990s, he started experiments in the field of atom optics. He developed a number of ways to coherently manipulate atomic beams, many of which, like the coherent energy shift of an atomic [De Broglie wave](/wiki/Matter_wave "Matter wave") upon diffraction at a time-modulated light wave, have become part of today's ultracold atom experiments. In 1999, Zeilinger abandoned atom optics for experiments with very complex and massive macro-molecules – [fullerenes](/wiki/Fullerene "Fullerene"). The successful demonstration of quantum interference for these C60 and C70 molecules[[41]](#cite_note-41) in 1999 opened up a very active field of research.

In 2005, Zeilinger with his group investigated the quantum physics of mechanical cantilevers.[[42]](#cite_note-42) In the year 2006 along with Heidmann in Paris and Kippenberg in Garching they demonstrated experimentally the self-cooling of a micro-mirror by [radiation pressure](/wiki/Radiation_pressure "Radiation pressure"), that is, without feedback.[[43]](#cite_note-43)

Using orbital angular momentum states, he was able to demonstrate entanglement of angular momentum up to 300 ħ.[[44]](#cite_note-44)

The founding took place in the local cathedral, which was later remodeled by [Caspar David Friedrich](/wiki/Caspar_David_Friedrich "Caspar David Friedrich") and his brother and can still be visited today. The founding of the university was made possible by a decree that restricted teaching activity at the [University of Rostock](/wiki/University_of_Rostock "University of Rostock") (founded 1419).
